title: Introduce Steadyhand egress gate: anticipatory throttle + soft quarantine for SLO-safe egress overloads
author: Aisha Raman
description: Motivation: we've observed short-lived egress oversubscriptions in eu-west and us-central during large batch replays and cross-region failover exercises. Those spikes cause transient SLO risk (95p latency violations) and aggressive circuit flips that cascade to downstream dependent services. This change introduces 'Steadyhand', an anticipatory egress gate that coordinates SLO enforcement, a region-aware circulator (soft circuit), and a graded load-shedding path to avoid abrupt failovers. Key goals: 1) reduce SLO violation risk during brief egress congestion windows; 2) avoid hard cuts (hard circuit opens) where a gentle throttled window preserves connectivity; 3) provide clear telemetry and a rollbackable rollout for on-call to revert quickly. Design summary: Steadyhand runs as a small control-plane daemon co-located with the regional router. It subscribes to existing capacity signals (egress_capacity_pressure, kv_pressure) and SLO-derived risk score from the global SLO enforcer. When pressure crosses a calibrated threshold it begins a two-phase response: (A) anticipatory throttle: progressively reduce burst allowance for non-critical tenants and mark requests with X-Egress-Mode:soft-throttle so downstream logging can correlate; (B) soft-quarantine window: place high-risk tenants into a timed probation with exponentially increasing backoff but still allow low-rate traffic to flow (avoids complete KV eviction). The mechanism integrates with circuit broker via a new 'softOpen' state which records a lease token and emits audit events to chronicle service decisions. Rollout plan: feature gate off by default; small canary in us-east-1 -> expanded to eu-west as metrics validate (SLO delta < 0.5pps). Emergency rollback: scripts/hotfix-rollout.sh toggles steadyhand=false and respawns router. Checklist: - [x] design doc and runbook written (docs/steadyhand.md) - [x] unit + integration tests (test/integration/egress_gate_test.go) - [x] telemetry and dashboards (observability: steadyhand/egress_pressure, steadyhand/slo_risk) - [x] API contract: X-Egress-Mode header and softOpen lease events - [x] rollout script and ops runbook commits summary: 1) initial control-plane and gate state machine 2) SLO enforcer hooks + risk scoring 3) circuit broker softOpen support 4) telemetry streams and dashboard definitions 5) integration tests and canary config changed areas/files: - cmd/steadyhand/main.go: new control-plane binary that drives the gate - pkg/slo/enforcer.go: add RiskScore API and minor refactor to expose windowed risk - pkg/circuit/broker.go: add softOpen/softClose transitions and lease metadata - pkg/egress/gate.go: throttle policy and tenant probation map - charts/steadyhand/values.yaml: canary/default config knobs - docs/steadyhand.md: runbook and dashboard links - test/integration/egress_gate_test.go: deterministic congestion simulator - scripts/hotfix-rollout.sh: emergency toggle and fast rollback samples Testing and CI: unit tests cover state machine transitions, deterministic TTL expiry, and header emission. Integration test simulates egress pressure and validates SLO delta and no hard-open circuit within the probation window. CI checks: lint (pass), unit (pass), integration (flaky -> fixed second run), e2e (pass on canary), bundle-sbom (pass). Observability: add steadyhand.egress_pressure gauge, steadyhand.slo_risk histogram, steadyhand.softquarantine_events counter. Backwards compatibility: the header X-Egress-Mode is opt-in; tenants not aware of the header observe no behavioral changes. Release notes: Steadyhand introduces an opt-in egress gate that provides smoother degradation under transient egress overloads and reduces the chance of hard failover. Ops runbook included in docs. Risks: mis-calibrated thresholds could cause unnecessary throttling — mitigated by conservative defaults and canary rollout. Long term: consider automatic learning of thresholds per tenant based on p99 tail latencies and usage patterns.
